# Levinas — Totality and Infinity (Lingis, 1969)

## Bibliographic identity

The selected English carrier is Emmanuel Levinas, *Totality and Infinity: An Essay on Exteriority*, translated by Alphonso Lingis (Pittsburgh: Duquesne University Press, 1969; The Hague: Martinus Nijhoff, 1969). French original: *Totalité et infini: essai sur l'extériorité* (The Hague: Martinus Nijhoff, 1961). This house was opened for the conjugate-field second pass (2026-09-07). Its bibliographic identity and its relevant primary locators are **verified through the Watson house's already-verified chain** ([Watson — The Resonance of Emptiness](../../../psychology/watson/watson-1998-resonance-of-emptiness/watson-1998-resonance-of-emptiness.md)), which transmits the Lingis edition and independently identifies pp. 49–51 and 197–201 as the relevant primary movement. No copy has yet been collated in hand; every quotation-level claim below remains a **lead until independently verified against the Duquesne printing.**

## Source scholarship

The work's movement, as the essay receives it: Western interiority tends to convert what is "not me" into what is "for me" — a world and its others represented, penetrated and managed within an economy of need. Levinas's central interruption is the relation to what exceeds that economy. The idea of infinity maintains a relation in which the Infinite exceeds the idea that thinks it; **Desire** names the infinite in the finite without possession satisfying it; the **face** is the Other's presentation as an overflow of the image held by the Same; and ethical resistance challenges the very exercise of power rather than opposing it as a larger force on the same scale. Responsibility here is prior to contract: the Other's claim arrives before any deliberation that would found it.

This summary is a paraphrase-level description transmitted through the Watson house's verified reading (its thesis at pp. 112–13, drawing on Gans's reading of Levinas); it is working orientation for the essay's consumption, not a substitute for the text.

## Essay use

### Source's relevant contribution

The love/face/responsibility register the conjugate root's A face draws: the face-to-face as the interruption of the economy of need; Desire as a movement that possession does not satisfy; responsibility as asymmetrical and prior. The root's facticity → dignity → love sharpening names this register as an **external refractor** of a claim the essay already argues on its own ground ([A35 Compassion](../../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A35-Compassion-Sensitivity-to-Origins-Epi-Logos-as-Vocation.md)'s non-devouring return; the non-possessive relation of the [A32 Reflective Field](../../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A32-Reflective-Field-The-Mirror-That-Moves-First.md)'s initiated return); the Watson house's earlier mapping — placing the face-to-face at the `AM/IS` determination, where first-person presence and third-person sayability meet through a second-person slash — remains the standing cross-register proposal.

### Licensed essay use

- Refract the ethic's ground (care resting on the fact of internality) through the face-to-face and responsibility-prior-to-contract, named as refraction.
- Join the need-to-desire transformation to the epi-logos vocation and the eros-of-logos candidacy's phenomenology register: encounter can revise the model and its value landscape rather than select an object within an unchanged egoic economy.
- Give unfamiliar agency (the xenophobia thread) an intimate register: reduction to a reassuring image or an exterminable image before the actual mode of agency is encountered.

### Claim boundary

Levinas warrants the ethical asymmetry, infinity, face, Desire and challenge to possession **within his phenomenological ethics**. The essay's mappings — `AM/IS`, the non-devouring return, the eros of logos, QL — are the project's own cross-register developments and must never be presented as Levinas's claims. The Watson–Gans chain's nested quotations remain double transmission until collated directly; this house inherits that debt explicitly rather than laundering it.
